Absolutely loved this trail. I listened to a few podcasts (GGB) and loved listening to the birds (Merlin app is amazing to help identify).  Many families out and especially along the river.   The sunset was beautiful.  A few new bridges being made.  Lots of paths and a few off course (watch for poisonous plants and ticks).  I saw a beaver ! For the first time outside of the zoo.  Met a man and his father who showed me how to identify the trees they’ve been chopping down after I showed them the beaver.   I wish I lived nearby so I could see the progress of the solo beaver ends up creating a dam with his chopping eventually.   A few bicyclist that need to learn to use their bell instead of nearly hitting you.   Overall I feel refreshed. I felt safe the entire time walking as a solo female.

this is a great trail in the heart of Oakville. While it is rated Medium difficulty, there are a lot of patches of the trail that are beginner friendly. It is my first ride here and I found a lot of small Jumps along the way that are  great for beginners.  One tip is if you find a patch that is too difficult for you, come back to the main wide trail and go further. I have seen different sections of the trail have different difficulty levels. hope that helps. have a fun ride. Cheers!!

Beautiful trail and so peaceful. Pretty easy for the most part, just come prepared with good boots or shoes. Note for any dog owners: though most of the dogs I encountered were leashed and well trained, I did encounter one that was off leash who had no recall. After asking the owners to get their dog, they told me it would be fine because, “he wouldn’t hurt me.” That’s well and good but it’s best to keep your dogs on leash here and respect another owner’s wishes when they ask you to leash your dog. Besides that experience, it was lovely and the perfect hike.
